units.summary: Mikko estimated that the company receives about 1,200 freight documents per day across all sites.
units.quote: My feeling is around 1200 a day, all sites together.

units.summary: A second meeting estimate put the number at around 1,000 on a normal working day based on the TMS document log; the log counts paper documents when they are scanned, so the count depends on how it is measured.
units.quote: I would say it's a bit less, maybe around a thousand on a normal working day according to the TMS document log. But the log only counts paper documents when they are scanned, so it depends on how you count.

units.summary: Six document clerks manually enter freight-document information into the transport system. Invoicing fields are also entered into Business Central.
units.quote: And then we have six document clerks, four in Vantaa, one in Tampere and one in Oulu, who type everything into our transport system by hand.

units.summary: Finding the shipment in the TMS takes about a minute, and entering document data takes 3–4 minutes, depending on the document.
units.quote: that takes maybe a minute. Then keying in the data, 3-4 minutes, depending on the document

units.summary: Invoicing fields are entered again into Business Central, resulting in double entry.
units.quote: And for the invoicing fields, they type them again into Business Central. So it's double entry.

units.summary: Miko estimated that about 4% of documents have an entry error, such as an incorrect weight, pallet count or reference.
units.quote: I estimate around 4% of documents have some error. Wrong weight, wrong pallet count, wrong reference.

units.summary: Document errors can lead to incorrect invoices, credit notes and customer disputes; finance staff spend about one day a week correcting them.
units.quote: That ends up as a wrong invoice, then a credit note, then a dispute with the customer. Our finance people spend about one day a week fixing those.

units.summary: Handwritten damage or reservation remarks on proof-of-delivery documents can be missed, delaying damage detection; the company has seven days to claim against a haulier under its terms.
units.quote: Then we notice the damage too late, and under our terms with subcontractors we have 7 days to make a claim against the haulier.

units.summary: 71% of proof-of-delivery documents were processed within two days of delivery, against a 95% target.
units.quote:
POD processed within 2 days of delivery
95 %
71 %

units.summary: The Vantaa TMS document log registered 15,126 freight documents in September 2026.
The monthly data extract records 724.6 hours of manual document entry for Vantaa in September 2026.
The data extract records 616 documents for which a later correction was made in TMS or Business Central for Vantaa in September 2026.
The operational extract includes 150 freight documents logged during a one-week time study across Vantaa, Tampere and Oulu.
units.quote: Document_Log_Sample - 150 freight documents logged during a one-week time study in Vantaa, Tampere and Oulu (28 Sep - 2 Oct 2026).

units.summary: The TMS has an API, but it supports one record at a time; bulk export is a separate paid service.
units.quote: One technical issue, the TMS has an API, but it only works one record at a time. Bulk export is a separate paid service.

units.topic: freight document proof of concept priority
units.summary: The advisors identified freight document processing as the best candidate for a first proof of concept, citing its volume and measurable baseline.
units.quote: First, we think the freight document processing is the best candidate for a first proof of concept. High volume, a clear baseline with clerk hours and error rates, and a clear business case.

units.topic: freight document proof of concept scope
units.summary: The advisors proposed initially testing one document type, proof of delivery, at one site, Vantaa, before scaling.
units.quote: We would suggest starting narrow, with one document type, the proof of delivery, and one site, Vantaa, and then scaling if it works.

units.summary: The proposed technical test is to use a sample of real documents, including poor-quality photos and handwritten remarks, and compare field-level accuracy with clerk entries.
units.quote: we would test a vision language model on a sample of your real documents, including the bad photos and the handwritten remarks, and measure field level accuracy against what your clerks entered.

units.topic: human review in freight document processing
units.summary: The proposed workflow sends only uncertain documents for human review, based on the model's confidence level.
units.quote: The human in the loop design is important, the model gives a confidence level, and only uncertain documents go to a person.

units.summary: For the workforce forecasting case, the advisors recommended a data assessment as the first step.
units.quote: Second, for forecasting, the first step is a data assessment.

units.summary: The advisors described customer-service email triage as technically easy but requiring the most compliance work, and suggested it as a second step after an AI usage policy is in place.
units.quote: Third, the customer service case is technically quite easy, but it has the most compliance work, so it's a good second step once you have an AI usage policy.

conflicts.description: The part 1 recording gives Mikko's estimate of about 1,200 documents per day across all sites. The part 2 recording gives a lower estimate of around 1,000 on a normal working day based on the TMS document log, while noting that paper documents are registered when scanned. The instructions give no source priority, so the estimates remain unresolved.
